memory_candidates.content: When reconciling records after a pull-request review round, re-verify every planning-time premise live (a `gh pr view`/`gh pr view --json files` sweep) immediately before the first edit, even a premise that already passed a research or planning pass. A merged PR can touch record files a plan's Risk table assumed it did not -- here, the premise '#7 is the only merged PR and it edited no record file' was false (the rewriting contribution's merged diff included two record files), discovered only by re-running the file-list check at implementation time rather than trusting the planning-time read.

In a 'Where the work sits'-style capability-to-record mapping table, the word 'contributed' can be an established convention meaning 'exists as a pull request's content, not necessarily merged to main' -- distinguished from 'merged', reserved for content actually on `main`. Before editing such a table to 'fix' a seemingly stale 'contributed' cell, check the table's own established usage across its other rows; several rows using 'contributed' for still-unmerged branch content is the convention working as designed, not drift to repair.

For a long task-description paragraph edited through `state-write.sh` (never by hand), the reliable pattern is: `jq -r` the current description to a scratch file, perform an exact Python string replacement (asserting the old substring is found, asserting the result differs), then pass the new full text back via `--arg desc "$(cat file)"` with a filter like `.active_projects |= map(if .project_number == N then .description = $desc else . end)`. `state-write.sh` has no `--rawfile` flag, so a file's content must go through `--arg` and command substitution, not a jq rawfile input.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic PR #7 (feat/proof-mode-rewriting)
sapience_notes.value: The merged rewriting contribution's own diff (3c7197f84) edited two record files, records/proof-mode-architecture.md and records/proof-mode.md -- contradicting a plan's premise that the sole merged PR in a five-PR review round touched no record file. A plan's own Risk-table assumption should be re-checked with `gh pr view N --json files`, not trusted from a prior research pass.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic records/proof-mode-architecture.md's 'Where the work sits' table convention
sapience_notes.value: The word 'contributed' in that table's capability-to-record mapping means 'exists as a pull request's content', not 'merged to main' -- distinct from 'merged', which is reserved for content actually landed. Rows describing an open, unmerged branch's content correctly use 'contributed', and are not stale text needing a fix.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic .claude/scripts/tests/test-deploy-baseline-lib.sh
sapience_notes.value: Its 'control: a genuinely matching warm-cache entry was expected to skip gate 1 but did not' case fails reproducibly (confirmed twice), each run in its own freshly created isolated tmp scratch directory -- so the failure is not a concurrency artifact of a shared specs/.gate-cache, but a standing, environment-specific defect in verify-deploy.sh's gate-cache warm-path logic itself, independent of any task's own file changes.
